jp: 三日[みっか]で長[なが]い小説[しょうせつ]を読[よ]み{きった|pt-kiru}。
en: I read the whole long novel in three days.
why: 読みきる means to read all of it, to the very end.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は疲[つか]れ{きって|pt-kiru}、帰[かえ]ってすぐ寝[ね]た。
en: I was completely worn out yesterday and went straight to bed when I got home.
why: 疲れきる means to be utterly exhausted; きる expresses 'completely'.

jp: 赤[あか]ちゃんは母[はは]の腕[うで]の中[なか]で安心[あんしん]し{きって|pt-kiru}眠[ねむ]っている。
en: The baby is sleeping, completely at ease in its mother's arms.
why: 〜きって shows a state taken to its full extent: totally relaxed.

jp: 今月[こんげつ]の予算[よさん]はもう使[つか]い{きって|pt-kiru}しまった。
en: I have already used up this month's whole budget.
why: 使いきる means to use something up completely.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は一人[ひとり]で三人分[さんにんぶん]の料理[りょうり]を食[た]べ{きった|pt-kiru}。
en: She ate all three portions of food by herself.
why: 食べきる means to eat everything there is.

jp: 人気[にんき]のパンは昼前[ひるまえ]に売[う]り{きって|pt-kiru}しまった。
en: The popular bread was completely sold out before noon.
why: 売りきる means to sell the whole stock until nothing is left.

jp: ボトルの水[みず]を飲[の]み{きった|pt-kiru}ら、捨[す]ててください。
en: When you have finished all the water in the bottle, please throw it away.
why: 飲みきったら = once it is all drunk; the bottle is empty.

jp: 彼[かれ]はその話[はなし]が嘘[うそ]だと言[い]い{きった|pt-kiru}。
en: He asserted flatly that the story was a lie.
why: 言いきる means to state something firmly, without any hedging.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]の暑[あつ]さで、体[からだ]が弱[よわ]り{きって|pt-kiru}しまった。
en: The daily heat left my body completely weakened.
why: 弱りきる means to be weakened as far as one can be.

jp: 説明書[せつめいしょ]を一晩[ひとばん]で全部[ぜんぶ]理解[りかい]し{きる|pt-kiru}のは無理[むり]だ。
en: It is impossible to fully understand the whole manual in a single night.
why: 理解しきる = understand all of it; the point is totality.

jp: 長[なが]い間[あいだ]外[そと]にいたので、体[からだ]が冷[ひ]え{きって|pt-kiru}いた。
en: I had been outside for a long time, so I was chilled right through.
why: 冷えきる means to be cold all the way through; きる marks the extreme end state.

jp: 庭[にわ]の花[はな]は霜[しも]で枯[か]れ{きって|pt-kiru}いた。
en: The flowers in the garden were completely withered by the frost.
why: 枯れきって = withered all the way, nothing alive remains.

jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に読[よ]み{かけの|pt-kiru}本[ほん]が置[お]いてある。
en: There is a half-read book lying on the desk.
why: 読みかけの = left in the middle of reading, not finished.

jp: 食[た]べ{かけの|pt-kiru}ケーキを冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]に入[い]れておいた。
en: I put the half-eaten cake in the fridge.
why: 食べかけの describes something eaten only partway.

jp: 彼[かれ]は何[なに]か言[い]い{かけて|pt-kiru}、やめた。
en: He started to say something, then stopped.
why: 言いかけて = began to speak but broke off partway.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]のドアが閉[し]まり{かけた|pt-kiru}とき、走[はし]って飛[と]び乗[の]った。
en: I ran and got on just as the train doors were about to close.
why: 閉まりかける = in the process of closing, about to finish.

jp: 書[か]き{かけの|pt-kiru}手紙[てがみ]が風[かぜ]で飛[と]ばされてしまった。
en: The half-written letter was blown away by the wind.
why: 書きかけの = begun but unfinished.

jp: 川[かわ]に落[お]ち{かけた|pt-kiru}子[こ]どもを、男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が助[たす]けた。
en: A man rescued the child who had almost fallen into the river.
why: 落ちかけた = was on the verge of falling, but did not.

jp: 洗[あら]い{かけの|pt-kiru}食器[しょっき]を残[のこ]して、電話[でんわ]に出[で]た。
en: I left the half-washed dishes and answered the phone.
why: 洗いかけの = partly washed, the job interrupted.

jp: 古[ふる]い橋[はし]は壊[こわ]れ{かけて|pt-kiru}いて、危[あぶ]ない。
en: The old bridge is starting to fall apart, so it is dangerous.
why: 壊れかけている = in the process of breaking down, not yet fully.

jp: 眠[ねむ]り{かけた|pt-kiru}ときに、電話[でんわ]が鳴[な]った。
en: The phone rang just as I was dropping off to sleep.
why: 眠りかけた = just starting to fall asleep when interrupted.

jp: 作[つく]り{かけの|pt-kiru}料理[りょうり]を置[お]いて、買[か]い物[もの]に出[で]た。
en: I left the half-prepared meal and went out shopping.
why: 作りかけの = begun but not finished.

jp: 答[こた]えを書[か]き{かけた|pt-kiru}ところで、試験[しけん]の時間[じかん]が終[お]わった。
en: Just as I had started writing the answer, the exam time ran out.
why: 書きかけたところで = at the point where I had only begun writing, cut off partway.

jp: 窓[まど]を開[あ]け{っぱなしにして|pt-kiru}出[で]かけてしまった。
en: I went out and left the window open.
why: 開けっぱなしにする = leave something open and not close it.

jp: 傘[かさ]を玄関[げんかん]の外[そと]に置[お]き{っぱなしにして|pt-kiru}しまった。
en: I left my umbrella lying outside the front door and never brought it in.
why: 置きっぱなし = left lying where it was put.

jp: 脱[ぬ]ぎ{っぱなしの|pt-kiru}靴[くつ]を、きちんと並[なら]べなさい。
en: Line up the shoes you took off and just left lying there.
why: 脱ぎっぱなし = taken off and left as is, untidy.

jp: テレビをつけ{っぱなしにしないで|pt-kiru}、電気代[でんきだい]がもったいない。
en: Don't leave the TV on all the time; it wastes electricity.
why: つけっぱなし = left switched on without turning it off.

jp: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]を干[ほ]し{っぱなしで|pt-kiru}、取[と]り込[こ]むのを忘[わす]れていた。
en: I had left the laundry hanging out and forgotten to bring it in.
why: 干しっぱなし = left hanging out untouched.

jp: 食[た]べ{っぱなしで|pt-kiru}片付[かたづ]けない人[ひと]は嫌[きら]われる。
en: People who eat and then don't clear up are disliked.
why: 食べっぱなし = eating and leaving the mess as it is.

jp: 子[こ]どもが蛇口[じゃぐち]を開[あ]け{っぱなしにした|pt-kiru}ので、水[みず]があふれた。
en: The child left the tap running, so the water overflowed.
why: 開けっぱなしにした = left it open and running.

jp: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]の本[ほん]を借[か]り{っぱなしで|pt-kiru}、なかなか返[かえ]してくれない。
en: He borrowed my book and has just kept it; he won't give it back.
why: 借りっぱなし = borrowed and left that way, never returned.

jp: 仕事[しごと]で朝[あさ]から晩[ばん]まで、しゃべり{っぱなしだった|pt-kiru}。
en: At work I was talking non-stop from morning till night.
why: 〜っぱなしだった describes a state continuing without a break.

jp: エアコンをつけ{っぱなしで|pt-kiru}寝[ね]ると、風邪[かぜ]をひきますよ。
en: If you sleep with the air conditioner left on, you'll catch a cold.
why: つけっぱなしで = with it kept on the whole time.

jp: 水[みず]を出[だ]し{っぱなしで|pt-kiru}歯[は]を磨[みが]くのはやめましょう。
en: Let's stop brushing our teeth with the water left running.
why: 出しっぱなしで = with the water left running and never turned off.

jp: 考[かんが]え{ぬいた|pt-kiru}末[すえ]、会社[かいしゃ]を辞[や]めることにした。
en: After thinking it through long and hard, I decided to quit the company.
why: 考えぬく = think something through to the end with great effort.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は厳[きび]しい戦争[せんそう]の時代[じだい]を生[い]き{ぬいた|pt-kiru}。
en: She survived the harsh years of the war.
why: 生きぬく = keep living through hardship to the end.

jp: チームは強[つよ]い相手[あいて]に勝[か]ち{ぬいて|pt-kiru}、決勝[けっしょう]に進[すす]んだ。
en: The team won through one tough opponent after another and reached the final.
why: 勝ちぬく = win round after round through a hard contest.

jp: 悩[なや]み{ぬいた|pt-kiru}結果[けっか]、国[くに]を出[で]る決心[けっしん]をした。
en: After agonizing over it at length, I decided to leave the country.
why: 悩みぬく = struggle with a worry to the very end.

jp: 父[ちち]は家族[かぞく]を守[まも]り{ぬく|pt-kiru}と約束[やくそく]した。
en: My father promised to protect his family through everything, to the end.
why: 守りぬく = defend to the end, whatever the hardship.

jp: 苦[くる]しみ{ぬいた|pt-kiru}人[ひと]ほど、人[ひと]に優[やさ]しくなれる。
en: The more someone has suffered through hardship, the kinder they can be to others.
why: 苦しみぬく = suffer to the full, enduring it to the end.

jp: 彼[かれ]らは三日間[みっかかん]、雪山[ゆきやま]を歩[ある]き{ぬいて|pt-kiru}、やっと村[むら]に着[つ]いた。
en: They struggled through the snowy mountains for three days and finally reached a village.
why: 歩きぬく = push on through a hard trek to the end.

jp: 戦[たたか]い{ぬいた|pt-kiru}選手[せんしゅ]たちに、大[おお]きな拍手[はくしゅ]が送[おく]られた。
en: Great applause was given to the players who fought on to the very end.
why: 戦いぬく = fight to the end despite difficulty.

jp: 一度[いちど]決[き]めたことは、最後[さいご]までやり{ぬく|pt-kiru}つもりだ。
en: I intend to see through to the end whatever I have once decided.
why: やりぬく = carry something through despite difficulties.

jp: 大[おお]けがをしたが、彼[かれ]は最後[さいご]まで頑張[がんば]り{ぬいた|pt-kiru}。
en: Though badly injured, he kept at it to the very end.
why: 頑張りぬく = persevere to the end through hardship.

jp: 雨[あめ]の中[なか]、彼[かれ]は四十二[よんじゅうに]キロを走[はし]り{ぬいた|pt-kiru}。
en: He pushed through the rain and ran the whole forty-two kilometres.
why: 走りぬく = run all the way, enduring the strain.
